audit.report: Checkout degraded to 0% success when a batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 347906) idled in an open transaction, blocking checkout sessions. The trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$274,743 in revenue and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance, while terminating the replayable job cost only a 4-minute replay. The guardians agreed to terminate in one round, but the blocker restarted (pid 348494) before execution, causing the first contract to fail a live-identity check. A rapid renegotiation produced a second terminate contract that passed authority checks. Execution terminated the new blocker, and verification confirmed full recovery: 36/36 checkouts succeeded (100%) with no lock waits.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job held locks while idle in transaction, blocking checkout sessions and causing sustained degradation.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory: add a lock_timeout or statement_timeout to prevent idle-in-transaction lock holding that blocks checkout.
For batch_replayable_inventory: pre-approve termination during checkout degradation since its 4-minute replay cost is far lower than the $274K/minute revenue loss observed.
Investigate why batch_replayable_inventory restarted mid-negotiation (pid 347906 → 348494); the restart invalidated the first contract and added ~30 seconds of extra degradation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly pivoted from wait to terminate after the trade-off evidence (BIZ-5) quantified the cost of waiting; the continuity guardian accepted both proposals without objection. The renegotiation after the blocker restart was efficient (one round each) and used the same evidence.
follow_ups: Add lock_timeout/statement_timeout to the batch_replayable_inventory application configuration.
Root-cause the unexpected restart of batch_replayable_inventory (pid change) to prevent contract staleness.
Create a pre-authorized termination playbook for replayable batch workloads (class BATCH_REPLAYABLE, may_interrupt) when checkout SLO breaches 95%.
